title: 2. 在场与从未成为现实态之物

zh: 2. 在场与从未成为现实态之物

en: An act always falls
time. Each single act is chronologically situated, either being earlier, later or concomitant to another act. It is inserted in an order of succession and converges in simultaneity. It belongs to a
(the series of alternating acts which correlate to each different ‘now’) and combines in the formation of an
(the ensemble of coexisting acts which correlate to one and the same ‘now’). The act falls

time because it is identified with, and qualifies, a ‘now’. Aristotle writes: ‘Actuality, then, is the existence of a thing not in the way which we express by “potentially” … we call even the man who is not studying a man of science, if he is capable of studying; the thing that stands in contrast to each of these exists actually.’
This other way of being is resolved in a temporal determination: the
scholar is he who, as well as being capable of studying, is studying
. The actual stands in relation to the potential as now does to not-now, as presence does to latency, and a circumscribed and measurable lapse of time in relation to an indefinite duration.
zh: 实现总是落在时间之中。每项具体实现都在年代上得到定位：它早于、晚于或同时于另一项实现。它被置入一个接续秩序，并汇入同时性。它既属于一个系列——与各个不同“现在”相关的一项项实现交替组成的系列——也参与组成一个集合——与同一个“现在”相关、共同存在的各项实现组成的集合。实现之所以落在时间中，是因为它同一个“现在”相等同，并规定这个“现在”的性质。亚里士多德写道：“现实态，就是一个事物不以我们所谓‘潜在地’那种方式存在……即使一个人没有正在研究，只要他能够研究，我们也称他为有学识的人；与这些情形分别相反的东西，则现实地存在。”
另一种存在方式最终归结为一项时间规定：现实的研究者不仅能够研究，而且此刻正在研究。现实态之于潜在态，犹如现在之于非现在、在场之于潜伏、范围明确且可以度量的一段时间之于不定的绵延。

en: To be actual means
. The term ‘actuality’, which in its common usage indicates the moment in which one finds oneself – today – has raised the hackles of purists, since given its provenance from
(and thus from

, ‘act’) it ought instead to designate the fulfilment of a possibility, the expression of a faculty: in sum, something being realised. And yet, from a conceptual point of view, this slide from the one meaning to the other is highly perspicacious. We must
grasp, within the term ‘actuality’, the compelling link between the ‘now’ and the exit from a state of potentiality. Only that which is
is, properly speaking,

. Acts take on the temporal prerogative of presence in virtue of their negative relation with the potentially existing (which, instead, is always latent and never actual). Precisely because they are no longer potential (that is, because they are no longer not-now), these acts are located within the progression of time along with so many other ‘nows’, establishing reciprocal relations of anteriority and posteriority. Whatever place it occupies in the flow of time, the act still has its own ‘now’, and still bears unaltered the stamp of presence (and is thus counterposed to the potential – and not, mind, to yesterday and tomorrow). The chronological past is made up of former
; the future, of
to come. The memory and expectation of an act are the memory and expectation of what was, or will be, essentially
zh: 现实地存在，意味着在场。“现实性”（actuality）一词在日常用法中指一个人所处的时刻——今天；这曾惹恼语言纯粹主义者，因为它源于 actualitas，进而源于 energeia（“实现”），照理应当指可能性的完成、官能的表达；简言之，指某物得到实现。然而从概念上看，从一个含义滑向另一个含义极其敏锐。我们必须在“现实性”一词中把握“现在”与脱离潜在状态之间强有力的联系。严格说来，只有得到实现的东西才是当下的（actual）。各项实现凭借同潜在存在的否定关系，取得在场这一时间特权；潜在存在则始终潜伏，从不成为现实态。各项实现恰恰因为不再是潜能——也就是不再是非现在——才同许多其他“现在”一起位于时间推进之中，并建立相互的在先和在后关系。无论在时间流动中占据什么位置，一项实现仍有自己的“现在”，也仍原封不动地带着在场的印记；因此，它所对立的是潜能，请注意，并不是昨天和明天。年代性的过去由昔日的现实性构成，未来则由将来的现实性构成。对一项实现的记忆和期待，就是对本质上曾经在场或将要在场之物的记忆和期待。

en: The act is always an object of perception. But the perception of an act is always, in the first place, the perception of a given temporal aspect or position. If we witness an event (for example, a house being built) without considering the categories of act and potential, then we will perceive it well enough in terms of its content; but if we understand the event which we are witnessing as an
(as something that has ceased to be potential) then the salient point is no longer the presence of a perception, but rather
. In the same way, if we refer to a chain of events in a series (for example, the notes of the melody to which I am listening) as a gradual series of
, we do not have so much a succession of perceptions, as a
The concept of the act, making explicit the presence or actuality of each event, offers perception the appropriate
for thinking the ‘now’ (or succession of ‘nows’) as such.
zh: 实现始终是知觉对象。但对一项实现的知觉，首先总是对某个既定时间面向或时间位置的知觉。假如我们目睹一个事件——例如一栋房屋正在建造——而不借助实现和潜能的范畴，那么我们仍能很好地知觉它的内容；但如果我们把眼前的事件理解为一项实现——理解为某种不再只是潜在的东西——关键就不再是知觉的在场，而是对在场的知觉。同样，假如我们把一个系列中的事件链——例如我正在聆听的旋律里一个个音符——理解为逐步现实化的系列，那么我们所拥有的与其说是一连串知觉，不如说是对接续的知觉。实现概念明确揭示每个事件的在场或现实性，从而为知觉提供一种恰当图式，使之能够把“现在”（或一连串“现在”）作为其本身来思考。

en: Still a problem, here, is the temporality of potential. Potential does not, as such, fall in time. What chronological measurement would be able to calculate the constant
of which potential consists? What place would be taken in the flow of ‘nows’ by the
to work or to build, the
of thinking or speaking, or the

to endure the cold or take pleasure from something? It does not seem possible to back up any coherent answer to this. It is true enough, naturally, that in many cases we do tend to locate potential within an empirical sequence, representing it as something that was there ‘just before’ (getting hot before it was burnt), ‘still’ endures (an old man still has the faculty of being able to procreate), or will emerge ‘later’. Still, we can easily see that the location of something potential within a determinate time is the consequence of a calamitous
: it happens, in fact, whenever this potential something is assimilated … to an actual one.
zh: 这里仍有一个问题：潜能的时间性。潜能本身并不落在时间之中。潜能由恒常的非现在构成；哪一种时序度量能够计算它？劳动或建造的能力、思考或言说的官能、忍受寒冷或从某物获得快感的禀赋，能在一个个“现在”的流动中占据什么位置？看来不可能为这些问题提供任何连贯答案。当然，在许多情形下，我们确实倾向于把潜能放进经验序列，把它表象成“就在之前”已经存在（某物在被烧灼之前先变热）、“仍然”持续存在（老人仍有生育能力）或“稍后”将会出现的东西。不过，我们很容易看出，把潜在之物定位于一个确定时间，是一场灾难性的张冠李戴（quid pro quo）的结果：只要这种潜在之物被同化为……现实之物，这种错置就会发生。

en: If we consider an actual thing (a block of marble) also to be, from a different perspective, something virtual (an artfully sculpted statue) then it might be said that this possibility does fall in time. But, on closer inspection, the marble is chronologically located only on account of what is actual about it. The date mistakenly attributed to the potential thing instead pertains to the act with which it coexists: whatever act that may be,
earlier or later than others of its own kind. Moreover, the potential appears to have a determinate temporal location when its concept comes to resemble – or is even
juxtaposed to – that of
or

. The causal relation, which undoubtedly implies a chronological scansion, does not concern potential, but only two or more acts. Aristotle writes: ‘from the potentially existing the actually existing is always produced by an actually existing thing, e.g. man from man, musician by musician; there is always a first mover, and the mover already exists actually’.
And while potential is certainly not the cause of anything, nor can it be said that it is inserted

time, taking on the appearances of an effect. The result of procreation is not a potential human, but an actual baby. The effect, as such, is always perfectly actual. The potential is the presupposition or collateral of the causal chain, surrounding it like an aura and providing the background to its unfolding: but in no sense is it a stage or component of this chain.
zh: 如果从另一个角度看，我们把一件现实之物（一块大理石）也视为某种潜在之物（一尊有待精心雕刻而成的雕像），那么似乎可以说，这个可能确实落在时间之中。但仔细看来，大理石之所以在年代上得到定位，只是因为它现实存在的那一面。被错误归给潜在之物的日期，实际上属于同它共同存在的那项实现；无论那是什么实现，它显然会早于或晚于其他同类实现。此外，当潜能概念近似于、甚至被并列于原因或结果概念时，潜能也会显得具有确定的时间位置。因果关系无疑包含年代分节，但它所涉及的不是潜能，而只是两项或更多实现。亚里士多德写道：“现实存在者总是由潜在存在者经由另一个现实存在者产生，例如人由人生出，音乐家由音乐家造就；总有一个最初的推动者，而推动者已经现实地存在。”
潜能当然不是任何事物的原因；同样，也不能说潜能以结果的外观被嵌入时间。生育的结果不是一个潜在的人，而是一个现实的婴儿。结果本身总是完全现实的。潜能是因果链的预设或伴随项，像光晕一样环绕因果链，并为它的展开提供背景；但它绝不是这条链上的一个阶段或组成部分。

en: Potential, as such, does not fall

time. Its texture – fully temporal, but not at all chronological – will escape the grasp of anyone who tries to snatch hold of it. For our purposes, we will limit ourselves, for the moment, to some intuitive observations, each of which we will later return to, examine, and radicalise. Let us pose ourselves the question of how a thinking person perceives her own capacity to think. She has the incontrovertible impression that this faculty precedes, accompanies and follows any particular meditation. Equally, the capacity to walk seems to exist before, but also during and after, any given stroll. And indeed, the capacity to speak is what remains when a series of acts of speaking have come and gone. The faculty resembles a uniform duration, a
that envelops and circumscribes

discrete units, single realisations. It is a bizarre duration, however: since it is never present, the capacity to speak is not spread out across a multiplicity of ‘nows’, and nor can it be broken down into (or measured in) lapses of time. If the act is ‘now’, potential is ‘always’: the former is evanescent, the latter is permanent. And yet, the ‘always’ of potential does not mean that it is perennially present, but rather

children: that it is perennially unable to coincide with actuality

en: . The potential is the persistent not-now against which each
is defined, the unmovable latency which constitutes the horizon (or context) of each dateable event.
zh: 潜能本身并不落在时间中。它的纹理完全属于时间，却丝毫不属于年代；任何试图一把抓住它的人都会让它从手中逃脱。眼下，我们只作几项直观观察，随后将逐一回到这些观察，考察它们，并把它们推向更彻底的程度。让我们提出这样一个问题：正在思考的人如何感知自己的思考能力？她会得到一种无可争辩的印象：这种官能先于、伴随并后于每一次具体沉思。同样，行走能力似乎存在于任何一次散步之前，也存在于散步期间和之后。事实上，一系列言说活动来去以后，言说能力仍然留存。官能近似于一种均匀的绵延，一条包围并圈定一个个离散单位、一次次具体实现的连续体。不过，这是一种奇异的绵延：言说能力从不在场，因此不会铺展在多个“现在”之上，也不能被拆分成或度量为一段段时间。如果实现是“现在”，潜能就是“始终”：前者转瞬即逝，后者恒久不变。然而，潜能的“始终”并不意味着它永远在场，而是意味着它永远无法同现实性重合。潜能是恒久的非现在；每个此时此地都以它为反面得到界定。它是不动的潜伏状态，构成每个可标定日期之事件的视域或语境。

en: But what is it that persists, without ever being actual? Even despite our initial considerations, here we must risk unequivocally choosing our line of march.

children: What persists as not-now is time as a whole

en: , all-embracing time, the entirety of time within which succession and simultaneity take place. It allows for becoming and change, but itself remains immutable. It is not expressed in a specific ‘now’, but nor is it the total sum of real ‘nows’. If it were actualised, time-as-a-whole would have to have chronological extension and progression, as well as a myriad of dates: in sum, it would itself fall
. To repeat: precisely because it is
, and thus perennially non-actual, time as a whole does not represent a ‘time before time’ (and another, and then another,
zh: 然而，那个持续存在却从不成为现实态的东西究竟是什么？即使前面的考虑还很初步，我们在这里也必须冒险明确选择前进路线。作为非现在持续存在的，是作为整体的时间，是无所不包的时间，是接续和同时性都发生于其中的时间总体。它使生成和变化成为可能，自身却保持不变。它不在某个具体“现在”中得到表达，却也不是所有现实“现在”的总和。如果作为整体的时间得到现实化，它就必须具有年代上的延展和推进，以及无数日期；简言之，它自身也会落入时间。再说一遍：作为整体的时间恰恰因为是潜在的、因而永远不处于现实态，才不代表一个“时间以前的时间”（也不会再在它以前出现另一个、再另一个，以至无穷）。

en: Augustine of Hippo, wanting to represent becoming with an – inevitably faint – likeness, compared the totality of time to a
text, and determinate times to parts of it, which are each in turn
(or which it is expected will be read):
zh: 希波的奥古斯丁想用一个难免不够贴切的比喻来表象生成变化，于是把时间总体比作一篇可供阅读的文本，把各个确定时间比作其中依次被读到（或预计将被读到）的部分：

en: I am about to repeat a Psalm that I know. Before I begin, my expectation is extended over the whole; but when I have begun, how much soever of it I shall separate off into the past, is extended along my memory; thus the life of this action of mine is divided between my memory as to what I have repeated, and expectation as to what I am about to repeat; but ‘consideration’ is present with me, that through it what was future, may be conveyed over, so as to become past … And this which takes place in the whole Psalm … the same holds in the whole life of man, whereof all the actions of man are parts; the same holds through the whole age of the sons of men, whereof all the lives of men are parts.
zh: 我将要背诵一首自己熟悉的圣咏。在开始以前，我的期待延伸到它的整体；但当我开始以后，凡从整体中分离出来、进入过去的部分，便沿着我的记忆延伸。于是，我这项行动的生命被分在两者之间：就已经背诵的部分而言属于我的记忆，就将要背诵的部分而言属于我的期待；但我的“注意”在场，借助它，未来之物被传递过去，从而成为过去……发生在整首圣咏中的事情……同样适用于人的整个生命，人的全部行动都是其部分；也同样适用于人类子孙的整个世代，所有人的一生都是其部分。

en: Time-as-a-whole is not the accumulation of lines recited, but rather the never-actual (that is,

recitable) psalm to which Augustine refers when he writes ‘before I begin, my expectation is extended over the whole’. What goes for the psalm is also true of any potential. If the totality of time must be represented as potentially existing, then, conversely, everything that exists potentially, entails the image of the totality of time.
zh: 作为整体的时间并不是已经背诵过的各行诗句的累积，而是奥古斯丁写下“在开始以前，我的期待延伸到整体”时所指的那首从未成为现实态——也就是仅仅可被背诵——的圣咏。适用于圣咏的这一点，也适用于任何潜能。如果时间总体必须被表象为潜在存在，那么反过来，一切潜在存在的东西都包含时间总体的影像。

en: The potential corresponding to an act of a given kind (the capacity to walk – a stroll; the capacity to think – a given meditation; the capacity to speak – a speech) portends the constant non-coincidence of actuality with time-as-a-whole. We cannot conceive the act in separation from potential, because we cannot locate a position of chronological progression without considering the persistence of time-as-a-whole; and conversely, we cannot conceive the potential in separation from the act, because
we cannot imagine time-as-a-whole if not on the basis of some passing location
time. We should not pass over in silence the crucial aspect of this question, one that demands deeper investigation in many further senses:

children: the potential is permanent, the permanent is potential

zh: 与某一类实现相应的潜能——行走能力对应一次散步，思考能力对应一次特定沉思，言说能力对应一篇讲话——表明现实性始终无法同作为整体的时间重合。我们不能脱离潜能来构想实现，因为如果不考虑作为整体的时间持续存在，我们便无法在年代推进中确定一个位置；反过来，我们也不能脱离实现来构想潜能，因为只有以时间中某个正在逝去的位置为依据，我们才能想象作为整体的时间。这个问题有一个要求从许多方面进一步深入研究的关键点，不应沉默略过：潜能是恒久的，恒久之物是潜在的。

en: The potential is not perceived. Due to its persistent inability to coincide with actuality (since it is the persistent not-now), it is, rather, an object of memory. In comparing time-as-a-whole to a potential psalm, Augustine specifies: ‘a Psalm that I know’. It is, then, a text to be re-evoked. It should go without saying, however, that it is necessary carefully to distinguish the memory of what was once actual (attached to the chronological past) from the memory of what has never been present (because it is irrevocably unable to coincide with actuality). To remember potential means to remember the time-as-a-whole within which the past ‘now’ falls, as does the actual ‘now’ and the ‘now’ that shall be. Such a memory accompanies and intersects each perceived actuality, no matter whether it be past, present or future. Above we said that perception provides the act with a
for representing its ‘now’. Here we must add that potential, for its part, constitutes the
through which memory touches on time-as-a-whole.
zh: 潜能不被知觉。由于它持久地不能同现实性重合——因为它就是恒久的非现在——它反而是记忆的对象。奥古斯丁把作为整体的时间比作一首潜在的圣咏时，特意说那是“一首我熟悉的圣咏”。因此，它是一篇有待重新唤起的文本。不过不言而喻，我们必须仔细区分对曾经现实之物的记忆——这种记忆附着于年代性的过去——与对从未在场之物的记忆——它不可撤销地无法同现实性重合。记住潜能，意味着记住作为整体的时间；过去的“现在”、现实的“现在”以及将来的“现在”都落在其中。无论被知觉的现实性属于过去、现在还是未来，这种记忆都伴随它并与它相交。前面说过，知觉为实现提供一种表象其“现在”的图式。这里还必须补充：潜能则构成记忆借以触及作为整体之时间的图式。
亚里士多德，《形而上学》第九卷，1048a 30—35。
